correctness.rationale: For \(a,b,c>0\) the isolated equilibria follow by exact elimination. Substitution into the Jacobian gives \(p(\lambda)=\lambda^3+(a+b)\lambda^2+(bc^2/a^2)\lambda+2bc^2/a\). The cubic Routh determinant equals \(bc^2(b-a)/a^2\), which proves Hurwitz stability exactly for \(b>a\) and two right-half-plane roots for \(0<b<a\). At \(b=a\) the polynomial factors as \((\lambda+2a)(\lambda^2+c^2/a)\). The showcased exact-arithmetic replay independently reconstructs the cubic and excludes a zero root.

evidence: Wang, Nonlinear Dynamics 60 (2010), DOI 10.1007/s11071-009-9601-1, studies \(\dot x=a(y-x)\), \(\dot y=cx-axz\), \(\dot z=xy-bz\) and gives a different isolated-equilibrium cubic.
Chen et al. replace the first equation by \(\dot x=yz-ax\); their symbolic local analysis on the same page is for the equilibrium line \(E_3\).
broader_coverage.reasoning: The natural stronger candidate is the stability theorem for the cited precursor. It is inapplicable because changing the first equation changes both the equilibria and their Jacobian polynomial, so its theorem does not dominate the present claim.

value.rationale: The result gives a sharp, complete positive-parameter local classification of the two nontrivial equilibria and identifies their unstable dimension, correcting a zero-eigenvalue spectrum in the motivating paper. The exact boundary \(b=a\) is structurally meaningful and lies inside parameter ranges studied in that work. The finding is stronger than a numerical recomputation while remaining self-contained and directly useful for interpreting local versus global dynamics.
